claims.claim: Continuity editing is an approach that organizes images and sound into a logical, legible progression that orients viewers in space and time.
Match-on-action, eyeline relations, transitions, screen direction, and master-shot coverage are among the techniques used to maintain continuity across shots.
Consistent screen direction helps establish a scene's geography by preserving a coherent apparent direction of movement and look across cuts.
The 180-degree convention uses an imagined axis through the action so coverage remains on one side, preserving apparent left-right relations until a re-establishing view changes them.
A master shot can establish the geography of a scene, while coverage supplies alternative views that can be selected and connected during editing.
Formal analysis can assess continuity by noting the smoothness or jumpiness of edits, transitions, shot relations, and their interaction with other elements of film form.
A strong continuity analysis describes what spatial or temporal relation a sequence establishes and then makes a qualified claim about the effect in context, allowing for deliberate disorientation.
